brief: Railway passenger seats; evaluating them for a regional train order.
summary: GRAMMER AG’s Americas business posted a €6.2 M operating EBIT loss in H1 2026, driven by higher logistics and tariff costs, and the company has flagged this as a key risk for the second half of the year.  At the same time, a 2024 loan renewal forces the firm to suspend dividend payments through 2027, signalling cash‑flow pressure.  Supply‑chain visibility is solid to Tier 3 via IMDS/RMI templates and a mandatory Supplier Code of Conduct, but Tier 4 mapping remains unconfirmed, leaving deeper sub‑tier blind spots.

report.headline: Limited sub-tier traceability beyond Tier 3 creates blind spots in GRAMMER AG’s supply chain

findings.text: Traceability coverage is tiered at -60, as the company utilizes the International Material Data System (IMDS) and RMI templates (CMRT/EMRT) to map material flows and conflict minerals through tier 3, though deeper tier 4 mapping is not yet confirmed as comprehensive.

While it uses digital risk management (SPHERA-SCM) for annual data updates, formal process audits (VDA 6.3) are conducted globally, and suppliers are required to perform their own internal audits at least once a year.

The company achieves a high tier (60) as its Supplier Code of Conduct (SCoC) has been a mandatory component of every digital RFQ since 2017, and 100% of global suppliers are required to confirm these policies, which include enforceable human rights and environmental terms.
Reporting zero confirmed incidents of corruption or human rights violations in the 2023 reporting year, supported by a strictly enforced SCoC and a digital whistleblower system.
Demonstrates a structured approach to ethical sourcing, primarily driven by compliance with the German Supply Chain Due Diligence Act (LkSG) and automotive industry standards.
